text:
Watches that count heartbeats and patches that measure blood sugar are becoming common, and I believe that wearable health technology will change patient monitoring considerably over the next twenty years, although it will not replace regular medical care.

First and foremost, wearable devices allow continuous monitoring outside hospital. Watches and patches record heart rate, blood sugar and sleep all day, warn of problems early and let patients with long-term illness manage their condition at home. A watch that detects an irregular heartbeat, for example, may prompt its wearer to see a doctor before a stroke occurs. Instead of a single reading in a clinic every few months, doctors will see trends over weeks, which gives a far more accurate picture of a patient's health. Hospitals could then send patients home earlier, with their condition watched remotely.

In addition, wearables will become smaller, cheaper and more powerful. Artificial intelligence will analyse the data and alert doctors only when something changes, so that patients get help in time and doctors are not overwhelmed. This approach is especially valuable for older people and those with heart disease or diabetes. However, there are limits. Some devices are not accurate enough for medical decisions, large amounts of data may overload doctors, and privacy and security of personal information are serious concerns. Older or poorer patients may also find the technology difficult or too costly to use. Training and subsidies would help to prevent a gap between those who benefit and those who do not.

In conclusion, wearable health technology is likely to change patient monitoring to a large extent by enabling continuous, remote and early detection, provided that accuracy, privacy and fair access are ensured.

plan.think: Ghi nhịp tim, đường huyết, giấc ngủ suốt ngày, cảnh báo sớm, bệnh nhân mạn tính quản lý tại nhà; bác sĩ thấy xu hướng nhiều tuần thay vì một chỉ số mỗi vài tháng; bệnh nhân về nhà sớm hơn. Ví dụ đồng hồ phát hiện nhịp tim không đều.

Thiết bị nhỏ hơn, rẻ hơn; AI phân tích dữ liệu và chỉ báo khi có thay đổi; giá trị với người già, bệnh tim, tiểu đường. Giới hạn: độ chính xác, quá tải dữ liệu, riêng tư, người già hoặc nghèo khó dùng.
Thay đổi ở mức độ lớn nếu đảm bảo chính xác, riêng tư và tiếp cận công bằng.
